sections.h2: What the Shiawassee County Register of Deeds does
sections.html:
Corunna's courthouse holds the land records for every parcel in the county. Incoming papers are checked against the state recording act, numbered, timed and indexed, and the originals are stored for safekeeping. A question about who owns a given parcel gets answered from this office's books.

Shiawassee's books start in 1836. From 1954 on, records are scanned into the computer system, and all of it can be searched by liber and page. The address is the Circuit Courthouse, 208 N. Shiawassee Street, first floor, Corunna, MI 48817. Phone 989-743-2216 or write rod@shiawassee.net.

The counter is staffed on weekdays, 8:00 a.m. until noon, then 1:05 p.m. until 5:00 p.m. The search room closes a little earlier in each half of the day. On county holidays the office asks visitors to phone and book an appointment, so call ahead before carrying in a closing package.

Recording is paid in cash or by check made out to the Register of Deeds. Card payment covers copies and searches, with a $1.00 convenience fee when you print from the website.

sections.h2: What it costs to record a deed
sections.html:
Recording one instrument costs $30.00. A deed that carries a warranty clause also needs a $5.00 tax certificate under MCL 211.135. The treasurer issues it from the second floor of the courthouse (989-743-2224). Land contracts, their assignments and condominium master deeds need the same certificate.

sections.h2: Michigan transfer tax in Shiawassee County
sections.html:
Recording a sale deed triggers a county tax under MCL 207.505 and a state tax under MCL 207.526. Shiawassee's schedule gives multipliers of .0075 for the state and .0011 for the county and tabulates the amounts in $500 bands. The first band, $100.00 up to $500, shows $3.75 state and $0.55 county.

  • Liability rests with the grantor.
  • The deed face shows total consideration and any claimed exemption.
  • A parcel crossing a county line splits the price between the two counties.
  • Stamps are sold only in the county of the land.
  • A Real Estate Transfer Valuation Affidavit carries no filing fee.

sections.h2: Transfers that are exempt from the tax
sections.html: The exemption list in MCL 207.505 excuses transfers priced under $100, mortgages and other security papers, leases, and spousal deeds that create or end a tenancy by the entireties. Relatives retitling a house commonly look at two items on that list: a corrective quitclaim, and a joint tenancy formed with someone who already owned the land. Ask the staff which subsection belongs on your deed.

sections.h2: What makes a Shiawassee County deed recordable?
sections.html:
The office posts a piece of Act 103 of 1937 (MCL 565.201) with its acceptance tests. Staff need the original paper with original signatures, a typed name under each signature, the grantee's address, a 2.5 inch blank band at the top of page one, and the drafter's name and address. The first five digits of any Social Security number must be removed.

A deed of unplatted land must also repeat the right-to-farm statement from MCL 560.109, warning that nearby farms may produce noise, dust and odors. When a spouse dies, the survivor brings a certified death certificate. No replacement deed is issued, since the office only records.

sections.h2: Sheriff's sales and other county offices
sections.html:
Sheriff's sales are held Wednesday mornings at 10:00 a.m. in the 35th Circuit Court lobby, and bidders need a certified check for the full opening bid. The office also links a property fraud alert service. Michigan leaves assessing and zoning to cities and townships, and the County Equalization department (989-743-2263) works across the county's 21 units of local government, fielding questions on valuation, millage and exemption status.

The county seat is Corunna, and Owosso is the largest city. Durand, Laingsburg, Perry and part of Ovid are the other cities. I-69 enters near the southwest corner and leaves east of Durand, and M-21 serves Corunna and Owosso.

sections.h2: Home values and ownership in the county
sections.html:
The 2025 estimate is 67,681 residents, against 70,648 in 2010. For 2020 through 2024 the county had 28,126 households, and owners occupy 80.1 percent of homes. The median value for a home lived in by its owner is $171,600. Median rent is $899, and median household income is $67,404.

At 128 people per square mile, most parcels sit outside a city street grid. A seller of rural land should expect the right-to-farm statement on the deed and may need extra time to gather a legal description.

sections.h2: Other county pages that help a seller
sections.html:
The Register of Deeds site links several pages worth reading before a closing:

  • A property fraud alert signup.
  • Sheriff sale information.
  • The county transfer tax exemption excerpt and the state exemption form.
  • The Michigan Homeowner Assistance Fund program at MSHDA, a starting point for owners who are behind on a mortgage.

The county treasurer collects and distributes tax roll levies for schools, townships, cities and villages, and its site includes a page for paying delinquent taxes online. Ask the treasurer for the balance on your parcel before you sign a purchase agreement, since the tax certificate on a warranty deed depends on those taxes being current.

sections.h2: Getting a deed ready for closing
sections.html: Give the title company or attorney your current deed and parcel details early. They draft the new deed with the full consideration or the exemption statute, add the drafter's name and address, and make sure the original signatures and notary are in place. For a warranty deed, the treasurer certification comes first. Then the signed original goes to the Corunna office, with the $30.00 fee, the $5.00 certificate and the transfer tax. A cash sale skips the lender, so the recording step is often the last thing between you and your funds. Ask the title company to confirm the transfer tax figure and the recording total in writing before the signing, and keep your recorded copy once the office returns it with the recording details stamped on it.

faqs.q: What will it cost me to put a sale deed on record in Corunna?
faqs.a: The filing charge is $30.00 per paper. If the deed has a warranty clause, add the $5.00 certificate from the treasurer next door, plus the state and county transfer taxes calculated on the price.

faqs.q: Is the buyer or the seller responsible for transfer tax in Shiawassee County?
faqs.a: The seller carries it. The county's posted schedule applies .0075 for the state and .0011 for the county against the price on the deed.

faqs.q: Will the office accept a scanned or photocopied deed?
faqs.a: No, it wants the signed original. Once it is on record, anyone can order a plain copy at $1.00 a page or a certified copy for an extra $5.00.

faqs.q: If my husband or wife died, do I receive a fresh deed?
faqs.a: No. Take a certified death certificate and the filing fee to the courthouse so the record shows the deceased owner is off the title. Your existing deed continues to apply.

faqs.q: How do I reach the Shiawassee County deeds office?
faqs.a: Go to the first floor of the Circuit Courthouse at 208 N. Shiawassee Street, Corunna, MI 48817, or dial 989-743-2216. On county holidays the office asks visitors to book an appointment.
